Introduce SafeRoute AI as an explainable decision support system for emergency evacuation. State that every recommendation can be traced to search, probability, or optimization logic.
A campus becomes a weighted state space
Graph nodes represent locations. Edges store distance and evidence-driven risk.

Explain the state-space representation: a person occupies one graph node, actions traverse edges, and the goal test checks whether an exit is reached. The path cost combines distance, Bayesian risk, and optional congestion.
Four search strategies reveal different tradeoffs
A* balances measured danger with progress toward safety.
* depends on graph and heuristic conditions

preview: Algorithm | Guidance | Complete | Optimal | Observed role

text: Briefly contrast uninformed and informed search. Emphasize that A star uses both accumulated cost and a heuristic. Mention that all four algorithms are implemented manually so the logic is visible for viva questions.
Sensor evidence becomes a transparent risk score
The risk weight λ lets the operator choose how strongly danger influences the route.
Explainability: every risky edge shows its probability, evidence and contribution to total cost.

Use the Bayes rule equation to explain why the model does not treat a sensor as perfect. Multiple observations update the probability of danger, and that posterior probability becomes a path cost component.
When an edge becomes unsafe, the plan changes
Run A* from the current node

alt: SafeRoute AI replanning interface showing an initial route and a changed route after a hazard update

text: Demonstrate the Replanning tab. Select an edge, increase its hazard probability, and apply the event. The system replans from the current position and displays both the old and new recommendations.
The optimizer tests exit combinations, capacity limits and corridor overlap before choosing a joint plan.

alt: SafeRoute AI multi-agent planning tab with three agents assigned to exits

text: Explain that planning agents independently can overload the same route. This module evaluates joint exit assignments and penalizes shared corridors while respecting exit capacity.
A genetic algorithm places scarce resources

alt: SafeRoute AI genetic resource placement optimizer

text: Describe the chromosome as a set of selected locations. Fitness measures weighted response distance. Selection, crossover, mutation, and elitism produce better placements across generations.
The system separates evidence, algorithms and explanation
Scenario controls, map editor, visual explanations
Nodes, edges, hazards, exits, agents and resources
Custom maps can be entered as tables
Walk from the interface down to the domain model. Emphasize modularity: each algorithm is independent and tested, while the UI only coordinates inputs and visualizes outputs.
20 search runs  •  5 scenarios  •  fixed seeds  •  CSV evidence

Use the chart to show that the fewest expanded nodes does not necessarily mean the best route. In the fire scenario, A star accepts a longer physical route to obtain the lowest combined distance and risk cost.
A complete, explainable AI course project

• Simulated sensor inputs

• Small graph model

• No crowd physics

• Decision support only
SafeRoute AI links course theory to a working system whose decisions can be demonstrated, measured and defended.
Close by mapping the project to the syllabus and stating the limitations honestly. Then invite the evaluator to choose a scenario for a live demonstration.
